name: Open rhinoplasty (columellar incision)

card.summary: Nose surgery performed through a small incision across the columella that lifts the skin to expose the whole tip, allowing precise reshaping of the nose.
card.note: Leaves a small columellar scar; swelling can take up to a year to settle.

quick.overview:
Open rhinoplasty adds a small incision across the columella, the fleshy strip between the nostrils, to the usual internal cuts. The skin is lifted so the surgeon sees the cartilage and bone directly and can reshape the tip and bridge.

People choose it to refine nose shape, tip definition and proportion with direct visibility, and it is commonly used for revisions and for grafting.
quick.how: Performed by a surgeon under anaesthesia, with the nose taped and splinted afterwards; the dressing is typically removed at about one week. Swelling can take at least a year to resolve fully.
quick.risks: Risks include visible columellar scarring, numbness or sensory change, prolonged swelling and the need for revision surgery. A systematic review found reoperation rates of 2.73% for primary open and 1.56% for closed, a difference that was not statistically significant.

lead: Open rhinoplasty is nose surgery in which a small columellar incision is added to the internal incisions, letting the surgeon lift the skin and see the cartilage and bone directly [1][2]. The approach improves surgical control and makes it easier to place grafts and refine the tip [1][2].
People use it to reshape nasal tip definition, projection and symmetry, which affects overall facial balance. Wikipedia reports it is usually preferred for revision rhinoplasty [2].
Open rhinoplasty has been traced to Rethi in 1934 and was advocated by Padovan and Goodman in the 1970s; a 1987 review noted the stigma of the columellar scar was slowly being put to rest [1][2].

chain: Columellar incision and skin lift exposes cartilage
Surgeon sculpts tip and bridge with full view
angle.text: The open approach gives direct visibility of the nasal framework, which people choose for precise tip refinement and grafting. The result is a permanent change in nose shape.

infobox: Tape and splint, removed at about one week [2]

paras: In closed rhinoplasty all incisions are inside the nose; in open rhinoplasty a columellar incision is added, giving better access to cartilage and bone and easier graft placement and tip refinement [2]. The incision is placed at the base of the nose and the scar is aligned to conceal it [2].

Rethi introduced an open approach in 1934, Padovan advocated it in the 1970s when endonasal surgery was standard, and Goodman helped popularise it [2]. A 1987 review reported surgeons increasingly using the technique and patients showing little dissatisfaction with the scar [1].

Closed rhinoplasty involves less dissection, swelling and scarring and faster recovery [2]. Wikipedia reports systematic reviews finding no significant long-term difference in functional or aesthetic scores, with the choice depending on surgeon expertise and anatomy [2]. A review of 49 articles found no difference in reoperation between primary open and closed techniques [3]. A randomised trial examined sensory changes in nasal subunits after each approach [4].
Swelling can take at least a year to resolve [2]. Sensory change in nasal skin is common after rhinoplasty [4].

A systematic review of 49 articles reported 7,902 primary open and 765 closed rhinoplasties and reoperation rates of 2.73% and 1.56% (p=0.071) [3]. A randomised trial compared sensory changes after open and closed rhinoplasty [4]. A 2022 randomised trial compared fast-absorbing and permanent columellar suture closure for scar outcomes [5].

timeline.event: Padovan and Goodman advocate open rhinoplasty [2].
Review describes growing acceptance of the open technique [1].
